title: Health aid for 2022
description: Aid to the health sector from each donor, split into basic and general health.
content: Basic health covers clinics, nutrition and disease control, and general health covers policy and hospitals.

title: Debt service relative to 2010
description: Each country's payments on external debt as an index of their level in the base year.
content: Each line starts at 100 in the base year, so a value of 150 means half as much again.

title: Concessional lending, 2005 through 2020
description: Loans with a grant element large enough to count as aid.
content: Pick a lender to show its loans alone.

title: Bilateral aid in 2019 prices
description: Amounts are adjusted for inflation to the price level of one year, so years can be compared.
content: Each donor's deflator comes from its own price index and exchange rate.

title: Private sector instruments
description: Loans, equity and guarantees that official agencies give to private firms.
content: Before 2018 these were counted at face value. From 2018 only the part that is a gift counts.

title: Loan reporting by donor
description: How each donor reports the loans it makes to developing countries.
content: Donors moved from reporting cash flows to reporting the grant element of each loan.

title: Each donor's newest reporting year
description: Each donor appears at the most recent year it has reported, which can differ between donors.
content: A grey bar means the donor has not reported for that year.

title: Pledges as of 2024
description: Money donors have promised to the climate funds, pledge by pledge.
content: Hatched bars show the part of a pledge that has been paid in.

title: Aid to small island states
description: Bilateral and multilateral aid to the members of the small island developing states group.
content: The line marks the year the SAMOA Pathway was reviewed, so aid on either side of it can be compared.

title: Food aid, 2021
description: Emergency food and food security aid by recipient.
content: Ethiopia and Yemen received the most food aid that year.

title: Debt statistics, 2024 edition
description: What poorer countries owe abroad, as the World Bank publishes it each year.
content: Each edition adds the newest year of data and can revise the years before it.

title: Water and sanitation aid by donor
description: Spending on drinking water, sanitation and hygiene, by the donor that gave it.
content: Darker blue means more aid.

title: Aid to tax administration
description: Support for revenue authorities, tax policy and customs.
content: The European Union gives more for tax administration than any other donor.

title: Kinds of debt relief
description: Ways creditors reduce what a country owes.
content:
- Rescheduling: payments are moved to later years.
- Write-off: part of the debt is cancelled.
- Swap: debt is cancelled in return for spending on a set aim.

title: Spending in the central Sahel
description: Aid to Burkina Faso, Chad, Mali, Mauritania and Niger.
content:
Three donors gave over half the total last year:
- France
- the United States
- the World Bank

title: Money sent home by migrants
description: Money migrants send home has grown faster than aid for most of the past decade.
content: Estimates come from central bank balance of payments records.

title: Imputed multilateral shares
description: The part of each donor's core funding to multilateral agencies that ends up in each recipient.
content: Each agency's spending by country is split back to the donors in proportion to what they paid in.

title: Top donors to education
description: Donors ranked by the aid they give to education in the year you choose.
content: Germany gives about USD 2 billion a year to education.

title: Newest reported year, by country
description: The latest reported aid for each country, with the year it refers to shown on hover.
content: Each country is shaded by the aid it received in its latest reported year.

title: UN appeal funding
description: Funding requested in UN appeals and the share of it met.
content: Appeals were the least funded on record, with under half of requests met.

title: Aid channels
description: The organisations donors route their aid through.
content:
The chart splits aid by who spends it:
- the public sector
- NGOs and civil society
- multilateral agencies
- the private sector
